reason: No cited evidence is provided to support any of the key premises about debinding atmosphere effects, gas evolution, oxide formation, retained carbon, or their impact on densification and mechanical properties in AlCrFeNiSi or similar HEAs. The claims rely entirely on uncited mechanistic reasoning.
premises: Oxygen-rich debinding causes oxide formation and rapid CO/CO2 gas evolution that induce cracking and impede interparticle diffusion in DLP-printed AlCrFeNiSi
Oxygen-deficient debinding reduces oxidation of resin and powder, limiting gas evolution and surface oxide formation
Retained carbon from resin in oxygen-deficient debinding facilitates earlier interparticle diffusion and bonding during sintering
Reduced gas evolution and oxide formation allow full consolidation at ~50 °C lower sintering temperature (1050 °C vs 1100 °C) with reduced cracking and porosity
